Against The Judgment And Award Dated:14.06.2017
Passed In Mvc No.124/2013 On The File Of The Senior
Civil Judge & Jmfc, Amact-14, Thirthahalli, Dismissing
The Claim Petition For Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
1.
The claimant is in appeal challenging the dismissal of the claim petition.

2. The case of the claimant is that her husband Mohamed Ashraf Musaliar was the pillion rider of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA/14-EC/0494 and the rider of the motorcycle lost control over the bike and hit the bridge of Seetha river which resulted in the death of both Mahamed Ashraf and the rider Samad.
3. The case of the insurer was that the claimant's husband was in fact the rider of the bike and Samad was the pillion rider.

4. Before the Tribunal, the Investigating Officer was examined as a Court witness and he also reiterated that as per the investigation carried out by him that Samad was riding the bike while Mohamed Ashtraf, the husband of the claimant was the pillion rider.
However, this evidence of the Investigating Officer has been discarded on the ground that no eyewitnesses to the accident had been examined before the Court.
5. When the insurer contends that the deceased was the rider and not the pillion rider, the burden of proving this fact would rest entirely on the insurer.

The insurer adduced the evidence of an officer,
who was admitted that he was not an eyewitness.
The only other evidence available was that of the Investigating Officer who reiterated that the deceased was riding pillion.

6. In an accident in which both the rider and pillion rider were killed and especially having regard to the fact that this was not a collusion between two vehicles, the expectation of the Tribunal that there ought to have been eyewitnesses to the accident would not be rational at all.
7.
Since it was incumbent on the insurer to establish that the deceased was riding the bike, the entire burden cannot be shifted on the claimant, who was the widow of the deceased.

If the insurer has not Sharabhi vs Samad @ Abdul on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46331114/
2 established its assertion that the deceased was riding the vehicle, the Tribunal could not have discarded the evidence of Inspector, who had investigated the entire incident and therefore, I am of the view that the finding recorded by the Tribunal that there were no eyewitnesses to the incident and therefore, it cannot be held that the deceased was a pillion rider, cannot be accepted.
8. Having regard to the evidence adduced by the Investigating Officer, it will have to be held that the deceased was in fact riding pillion.
9. As far as compensation is concerned, there is no evidence indicating the actual income of the deceased.

As there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year, 2012 would be Rs.7,000/-.
10. Since the deceased was aged 27 years, 40% requires to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.9,800/-.
If 50% is deducted towards personal expenses, his monthly income would be Rs.4,900/-.
11. The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.4,900/-.
12. As the deceased was aged 27 years, a multiplier of '17' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.9,99,600/- (Rs.4,900 x 12 x 17) towards "loss of dependency".
13.

The claimants being the widow, she would be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards "loss of consortium"
and she would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

14. Thus, the claimant, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 9,99,600
2 . Loss of Consortium 44,000
3. Conventional Heads 33,000  Total 10,76,600

3 15.
Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.10,76,600/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment before this Court.

17. On such deposit being made, the claimant would be entitled to withdraw 50% of the compensation and the balance 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized Bank of her choice, initially for a period of five years, with liberty to withdraw accrued interest periodically.
18. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
